perspective:
**Christian Mensah’s available information:**

- He is a Black male police officer with a high-school education. He knows Jonathan Balogun as his childhood best friend, a carpenter with a master’s degree; Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Christian felt Jonathan was hiding something important, which made him anxious and suspicious. He arranged to meet Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- At the meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt something was being hidden and that Jonathan had been acting differently. He heard Jonathan admit he was in some trouble and had kept it from Christian because he didn’t know how to tell him.
- Christian told Jonathan he was worried and offered to help, saying they could face it together. He heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated and he didn’t want to drag Christian in. Christian insisted he was his best friend and would help. Jonathan said he could use support and resources and needed to figure a way out of the mess.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it involved anything illegal. He heard Jonathan say he couldn’t be sure, might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but did not do anything illegal himself. Christian said he wanted to make sure Jonathan was safe and would look into it discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian learned or concluded that Jonathan was being framed by someone trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this, said he had leads but did not yet name the framer, and decided to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian later identified/believed the real culprit was someone close to both him and Jonathan—someone they both know and trust. He told Jonathan he found out who was behind it and planned to confront them and bring them to justice, saying the betrayal would not go unpunished. He heard Jonathan warn him the person is dangerous but express trust that Christian would do what is right.
